www_home_hero_heading: {#gradient}{years} years{/gradient} of connecting students to meaningful work.
www_home_hero_body: CodeDay has been connecting education to real-world work since 2009. In our programs, students learn to build for real users long before anyone thinks they're capable.
www_home_announcement_deadline_text: Applications for year-long career prep end soon.
www_home_logowall_heading: Our alumni are building the future.
www_home_logowall_subhead: CodeDay alumni work for every leading tech company, including:
www_home_logowall_disclaimer: {name} and the {name} logo are trademarks of {legalName}.
www_home_impact_aggregate_label: {count} projects created at our events and online programs.
www_home_formats_heading: We help students build for real users long before anyone thinks they're ready.
www_home_formats_body: Our programs start in middle school, and last until students graduate college. As they improve, the work gets longer and the stakes get higher. By the time they graduate, they're designing and shipping features for millions of users.
www_home_formats_event_body: Pitch the thing you want to make on Saturday morning. Build it with a team. By Saturday night, people who have never met you will see it work.
www_home_formats_microinternship_body: One real issue in a project people actually use, a mentor who has done this before, and a maintainer who will merge your fix or tell you why not.
www_home_formats_microinternship_route_o: Year-long program. Apply as an individual.
www_home_formats_microinternship_route_c: Participate inside your college's course for credit.
www_home_formats_residency_body: You already shipped a fix a maintainer merged. Now find what the project needs next, make the case to the people who run it, and build it. They can say no. You keep going until it is in.
www_home_formats_residency_info_body: Residency spots aren't applied for — students are invited based on how they showed up during a Micro-Internship.
www_home_impact_heading: Our students ship code to real users while they're in school.
www_home_impact_body: Every project below has real users. For beginners, the users are their friends and community, but by their junior year of college, students are shipping into real projects with millions of users.
www_home_history_heading: {number} years of starting from what students need and building the program from there.
www_home_history_body: CodeDay was founded in 2009 by high school students who wanted to bring meaningful work into education. The design has changed many times, but what students do is the same: find something somebody needs, learn on their own, and build something that people will really use.
www_home_whymatters_heading: Entry-level jobs now ask for senior-level thinking.
www_home_whymatters_body: {#p}AI does most entry-level work now. The bar for today's graduates is far higher. Jobs where graduates can expect detailed, clear assignments and hand-holding are going away.{/p}{#p}Today's graduates must find what is worth building, learn new fields, decide what context is relevant, and review results. CodeDay has been producing these students since 2009.{/p}{#p}If that becomes normal instead of lucky, the ordinary twenty-two-year-old is capable of what only the exceptional one is today.{/p}
www_home_stats_alumni_provenance: Online + in-person at {eventCount} events across {citiesCount} cities
www_home_stats_lowincome_label: Come from low-income households, where a tech job is life-changing
www_home_stats_lowincome_provenance: Combination of self-reported and school data
www_home_stats_econvalue_label: Lifetime earnings gain for students who were otherwise unlikely to get a tech job
www_home_stats_econvalue_provenance: Or {otherNonprofits} if we counted the full salary of every participant, as most nonprofits do
www_home_evidence_heading: We publish peer-reviewed research on how our approach works, why it works, and how well it works.
www_home_evidence_body1: {#p}We rigorously study what we run in-house and commission independent evaluations. Then we publish the findings where other researchers can check the work. Our programs evolve in response to what the evidence says, even when it's hard.{/p}{#p}While our vision has stayed the same since 2009, the design has changed many times, which is why our programs are so effective.{/p}
www_home_waysin_colleges_body: Colleges work with CodeDay to help students learn the higher-order skills they need to get a job today. Our programs integrate into a class or capstone, or can be extra-curricular.
www_home_waysin_companies_body: Companies hire from CodeDay because our "entry-level" graduates are already close to mid-level engineers.
www_home_waysin_foundations_body: Join us in building the future of education.
www_home_waysin_mentors_body: Your commitment will make a life-long impact for students, and most commitments are only a few hours.
www_home_waysin_maintainers_body: We'll help you gain a steady supply of long-term contributors (who don't just produce vibe-code slop).
www_home_meta_description: CodeDay puts students in front of real, unfinished work — an event, a micro-internship, a term, or longer — reviewed by the maintainers who need it done.

www_research_hero_standfirst_before: Many nonprofits make claims. CodeDay provides evidence. We've published
www_research_hero_standfirst_count: {count} peer-reviewed papers, evaluation reports, and datasets
www_research_hero_standfirst_after: on open-source mentoring, hackathon persistence, GenAI in software work, and what employers actually hire for. Every paper, preprint, evaluation report, talk and dataset is listed below.
www_research_stat_papers_label: peer-reviewed papers, evaluation reports, and datasets
www_research_empty: Nothing matches. Clear the search or pick another type.
www_research_closing_heading: Our programs are open to study.
www_research_closing_body: Our team co-authors with researchers as well as commissions independent evaluations. If you want to test a question against twenty years of student outcomes, start here.
www_research_closing_researchers_body: We work with researchers to test interventions; provide access to de-identified program data; and make students, alumni, and mentors available for interviews.
www_research_closing_evaluators_body: We've commissioned independent evaluations rather than grading our own work. Contact us if you'd like access to evaluation instruments and data.
www_microinternship_meta_description: One real issue in a project people actually use, a mentor who has done this before, and a maintainer who will merge the fix or say why not. Open year-round for students 13 and up.
www_microinternship_hero_heading_after: to software the industry runs on.
www_microinternship_hero_body: Solve a real issue in a project people actually use with a mentor who has done this before
www_microinternship_hero_card_pr_title: Fix flaky timeout in the scheduler test suite
www_microinternship_hero_card_pr_body: Replaces a fixed sleep with a polling wait so the test passes under CI load. Closes #4790.
www_microinternship_hero_card_mentor_age: Agenda: what to build next, and how to write this PR into a resume.
www_microinternship_how_heading: One real issue, from first read to merge, in one to two months.
www_microinternship_how_week1_body: In the first week, each student is matched to one open issue in a live project + an industry mentor, then participates in training to learn how to get up-to-speed on an existing project.
www_microinternship_how_following_headin: Two meetings a week, one owner
www_microinternship_how_following_body: Every week has one team meeting and one mentor meeting, with a guided agenda. (Mentors offers guidance, but they do not take over.) Additional help is available upon-request from our team of Consulting Software Engineers.
www_microinternship_how_done_body: Your work is finished when you submit your contribution to the project. While you wait for a maintainer to review it, we'll help you write a reflection on what you learned and share your experience with your professional network.
www_microinternship_afterward_body: Because our partner projects are widely used and recognized by industry, we encourage you to share your contributions and what you've learned! The project comes first, then what you shipped, and its impact. Anyone reading it can open your pull request and see the contribution and maintainer review for themselves.
www_microinternship_afterward_hiring_lin: Peer-reviewed studies of hiring managers found they were willing to interview candidates based on open source experience.
www_microinternship_afterward_resume_sum: Fixed a flaky timeout in the scheduler test suite; merged and released in v[X.Y].
www_microinternship_afterward_resume_quo: I did a CodeDay Micro-Internship with [Project].
The sentence students use when someone asks.
www_microinternship_register_heading: Register with a school or individually.
www_microinternship_register_body: Schools that partner with CodeDay run their own cohorts. Everyone else can register on their own for our year-long cohort.
www_microinternship_register_school_body: Many colleges partner with CodeDay to offer micro-internships as an extracurricular or integrated into a course or capstone. If you were sent a link from your school, you must click it to register.
www_microinternship_register_school_part: Not sure if your school partners with CodeDay?
www_microinternship_register_own_body: Students who don't attend a participating school can participate in our year-long program offered with our partner Mentors in Tech.
www_microinternship_register_own_check1: 2 to 3 micro-internships, each a merged contribution
www_microinternship_register_own_check2: Monthly meetings with two industry career mentors
www_microinternship_register_own_check3: Summer CodeDay Residency (if all requirements met)
www_microinternship_register_partner_pro: Would you rather your school offered this? Let them know.
www_microinternship_evidence_heading: The design comes from published research. So do the results.
www_microinternship_evidence_body: Independent evaluations of our program and our own research come to the same conclusion: working on real projects with industry supervision helps develop the higher-order thinking common in mid-to-senior level engineers, and increases job outcomes.
www_microinternship_individual_meta_desc: Register a student directly for the CodeDay Micro-Internship: pay at checkout or apply for a scholarship. Same micro-internships, same mentors, same Residency invitation.
www_microinternship_individual_breadcrum: Work experience and career mentorship for CS college students

www_microinternship_individual_title_bod: Individuals are invited to participate in our year-long program, offered in partnership with Mentors in Tech.
www_microinternship_individual_stats_stu: Students have participated in the program
www_microinternship_individual_stats_job: More likely for students in the program to get a job, compared to peers
www_microinternship_individual_stats_men: Combined years of experience from our 1,000 industry mentors
www_microinternship_individual_title_sch: Registering with a college or school?
If your school asked you to apply for a CodeDay micro-internship or capstone, do not apply for this program. Use the link your school gave you instead.
Learn more about our school programs
www_microinternship_individual_things_he: One year of career mentorship and open source work experience.
www_microinternship_individual_things_mi: {#p}1-2 months each. Your choice of October, November-December, January-February, March, April, May, or June.{/p}{#p}Each micro-internship will help you ship a contribution to a popular open source software project, and ends with a Github contribution you can include on your resume and a blog post shared on LinkedIn.{/p}
www_microinternship_individual_things_me: {#p}At the start of the program, you will be matched with two career mentors, who are engineers with a long career in industry.{/p}{#p}Each month, you'll meet with each of them 1-1. The agenda covers topics like the job search, LinkedIn and resume glow-up, prepping for interviews, and negotiating offers.{/p}{#p}Your mentors will also help you track your job applications. Students are expected to apply to several jobs each month.{/p}
www_microinternship_individual_things_wo: Each month, you will attend a workshop to help you navigate your job search, and have access to office hours with our network of career experts.
www_microinternship_individual_things_re: Students who meet every requirement but do not secure an internship or job offer are invited to a summer Residency, where you will ship a far more complex contribution to an industry-recognized project. (Must have met all previous program requirements to qualify.)
www_microinternship_individual_options_b: {#p}Paid registration covers two seats: one for your student, and one for a student whose family cannot pay.{/p}{#p}Most CodeDay students come from families who could not afford a program like this, and we do not turn students away over money. If the cost is a barrier for your family, apply for a scholarship. Nobody in the cohort knows who paid and who did not.{/p}
www_microinternship_individual_options_p: The full program is $6,000 per year. This covers your cost + the cost to provide the program to another student whose family cannot afford it.
www_microinternship_individual_options_s: The cost is covered for families who need it. Scholarships are funded by paid registration as well as CodeDay's sponsors.
www_events_hero_intro: A game for your friends, a tool for your school, an answer to something your neighborhood keeps asking about. Pitch the idea, build it with mentors in the room, and demo it when time is up. CodeDay Events run in {cityCount} cities, each on its own schedule. A quarter of the people who come have never written code.
www_events_showcase_link: See hundreds more on the Showcase →
www_events_picker_intro: Every city sets its own dates. Choose one to see its dates, venue, and registration. Cities on an interest list have no event planned yet; enough interest is how one gets planned.
www_events_no_results_body_pre: Join the interest list and we will tell you when one is planned, or
www_events_volunteer_link: Mentor or volunteer at this event
www_events_volunteer_line_post: CodeDay {city} is organized by local volunteers.
www_events_organize_body: Every CodeDay Event is run by local volunteers with CodeDay's playbook, venue partners, and staff support, on whatever dates work for them. Tell us where you are and we will connect you with the people already planning one, or help you start it.
www_events_organize_schools: Schools and companies can also host a venue.
www_events_steps_intro: The same four steps in every city, with mentors and event staff in the room the whole time. How long it runs is up to the city.
www_events_steps_1_body: Anyone can stand up and pitch a game, an app, or a tool they want to make. Big, small, silly, or serious, every idea gets a hearing.
www_events_steps_2_body: Teams form around the ideas people want to build. Beginners join people who have done this before, so nobody builds alone.
www_events_steps_3_body: Mentors move between teams the whole time. The only classes are a few optional hour-long workshops on games, music, apps, and interactive stories.
www_events_steps_4_body: Every team shows what works, finished or not. Of students who did not plan to pursue coding before CodeDay, 69% were still working on projects afterward.
www_schoolpartnership_meta_description: Ask your dean or school administrator whether your school is going to offer the CodeDay Micro-Internship. Copy a sample email and send it their way.
www_schoolpartnership_heading: Bring the Micro-Internship to your school.
www_schoolpartnership_body: Want your school to offer the CodeDay Micro-Internship as a club, part of a class, or a senior capstone? The easiest way to get things moving is to ask. Below is a sample email you can send straight to your dean or another administrator.
www_schoolpartnership_instructions_body: Copy the email below, paste it into a new message to your dean, and swap in your own name and school. Feel free to tweak it so it sounds like you. Want a different one? Hit shuffle.
www_schoolpartnership_template_1_subject: Are we doing the CodeDay Micro-Internship?
www_schoolpartnership_template_1_body:
Hi [Dean's Name],

Have you seen CodeDay's Micro-Internship program? Students get matched with an industry mentor and spend a month or two fixing a real issue in an actual open-source project, kind of like a mini internship. Schools can run it as a club, plug it into an existing class, or use it as a senior capstone.

Is this something we're going to do here? I'd want to be in the first group if we are.

Thanks,
[Your Name]
www_schoolpartnership_template_2_subject: Idea for a capstone - CodeDay Micro-Internship
www_schoolpartnership_template_2_body:
Hi [Dean's Name],

I came across something called the CodeDay Micro-Internship and thought it could be a good capstone option, or even just an extracurricular. Students get paired with a mentor from industry and actually contribute to a real project, not just a class assignment.

Are we planning to look into bringing this to [School Name]? I can send over more info if that helps.

[Your Name]
www_schoolpartnership_template_3_subject: Could this be a club or class thing?
www_schoolpartnership_template_3_body:
Hey [Dean's Name],

Quick question - have you looked into CodeDay's Micro-Internship program? It's a structured way for students to work on real open-source projects with an industry mentor, and schools can run it as a club, build it into a course, or use it as a senior capstone.

Is this something we're offering? I think a lot of people here would sign up if we did.

Thanks!
[Your Name]
www_schoolpartnership_template_4_body:
Hi [Dean's Name],

I found this program called the CodeDay Micro-Internship where students get matched to a real open-source project and an industry mentor for a month or two. It looks like it could work as an extracurricular, part of an existing class, or a capstone project.

Do you know if this is something we're doing, or could look into? Let me know who I should talk to if that helps move it along.

Best,
[Your Name]
www_schoolpartnership_template_5_body:
Hi [Dean's Name],

Have you heard of CodeDay's Micro-Internship? Students work on a real issue in an actual open-source project with an industry mentor, and it's set up so schools can offer it as a club, fold it into a class, or use it for a capstone.

Are we planning on doing something like this? If not, is it something we could start looking into?

Thanks,
[Your Name]
